whyOthersWrong: Language is controlled by prompt, not parameters; parameters don't change training data; length is controlled by max_tokens.
trap: Using high temperature for factual tasks (where determinism matters) or low temperature for creative tasks (where variety matters).
mnemonic: Low temp/top_p = focused/factual, High temp/top_p = diverse/creative

domain: Implement Generative AI and Agentic Solutions
stem: When defining an AI agent, why is "conversation tracking" important?

options.label: B
options.text: To maintain context across multiple conversation turns, track the progress of multi-step tasks, and enable the agent to reference earlier parts of the conversation when making decisions

options.label: C
options.text: To count the total number of conversations

hint: Without tracking, every message is a fresh start — the agent forgets what happened before.
explanation: Conversation tracking maintains state across turns — what was discussed, what tasks are in progress, what the user's preferences are. AI-103 covers defining "conversation tracking methods" as part of agent design.
whyOthersWrong: Billing is a separate concern; conversation counting is analytics; network monitoring is infrastructure.
trap: Implementing stateless agents for multi-turn tasks — without conversation tracking, the agent can't maintain coherent multi-step workflows.
mnemonic: Conversation tracking = the agent's short-term memory across turns

stem: What type of analysis can Azure AI perform on video content?

options.label: A
options.text: Only counting the number of frames

options.label: B
options.text: Frame-by-frame visual analysis, object detection, scene understanding, text extraction from video frames, and combined audio-visual analysis

hint: Video is a sequence of images plus audio — AI can analyze both modalities.
explanation: Azure AI video analysis processes both visual and audio components — extracting information from frames (objects, text, scenes) and audio (speech, sounds). AI-103 covers video analysis as part of computer vision solutions.
whyOthersWrong: Frame counting is trivial; video-to-audio is conversion, not analysis; compression is encoding, not AI analysis.
trap: Treating video analysis as just "images in sequence" — the audio component and temporal dimension add significant analysis capabilities.
mnemonic: Video analysis = visual (frame by frame) + audio (transcription, sounds) + time

stem: A financial services company is developing a credit card fraud detection system. Since "normal transactions" account for 99.9% of all card transactions while "fraudulent transactions" make up only 0.1%, the team finds that if the model predicts all transactions as normal, accuracy still reaches 99.9%, but this completely fails to meet business goals. The business team emphasizes: "Missing any fraudulent transaction (false negative) would cause extremely high financial losses, so we must capture all potential fraud." What metric should be prioritized when evaluating this model?
hint: This is a fundamental ML concept question.
explanation: In highly imbalanced datasets (like fraud detection, disease diagnosis), the cost of missing positive cases (false negatives) is extremely high. Recall is defined as TP / (TP + FN), specifically measuring the model's ability to capture all actual positive cases. Optimizing Recall ensures as few fraudulent transactions as possible are missed. Precision measures how many predicted positives are truly positive, while Accuracy gets skewed by the non-fraud majority class.
whyOthersWrong: A) Precision — does not address the specific requirement described in the question. C) Accuracy — does not address the specific requirement described in the question. D) Mean Absolute Error — does not address the specific requirement described in the question.
trap: "Precision" is easily confused; choose "Recall".
mnemonic: 正常交易 → Recall

stem: Which of the following best describes the concept of "embedding"?

options.text: Technology for converting text to speech

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Technology for compressing large models into smaller ones

options.text: A method for merging multiple models into one

options.label: B
options.text: Converting data (text, images, etc.) into high-dimensional vector numerical representations**

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question
explanation: Embedding maps discrete data to a continuous vector space where semantically similar data points are close together. It is the foundation for RAG, semantic search, and similar applications.
whyOthersWrong: A) Text-to-speech — that's Amazon Polly. C) Model compression — that's distillation or pruning. D) Merging models — that's model ensembling.
trap: "Converting text to speech" is a distractor; choose "Converting data to high-dimensional vectors"

stem: Regarding generative AI hallucination, which description is most accurate?

options.text: Hallucinations only occur when using poor prompts

options.label: B
options.text: The model produces content that seems plausible but is actually incorrect or fabricated

options.label: C
options.text: Hallucinations can be completely eliminated by increasing model size

options.label: D
options.text: Hallucinations only appear in text generation, not in image generation

options.label: B
options.text: The model produces content that seems plausible but is actually incorrect or fabricated**

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question
explanation: Hallucination is an inherent limitation of LLMs that cannot be completely eliminated. Any prompt can trigger it, and it occurs in both text and image generation.
whyOthersWrong: A) Only with poor prompts — can happen with any prompt. C) Eliminated by larger models — cannot be fully eliminated. D) Text only — also occurs in image generation.
trap: "Only with poor prompts" is a distractor; choose "plausible but incorrect content"

stem: Which of the following is a common communication pattern in multi-agent systems? (v1.1 new exam point)

stem: Which two are known limitations of generative AI?

stem: A law firm wants AI to answer client questions based on the latest regulations. Regulations are updated weekly and sources must be cited. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Perform full pre-training of the foundation model

stem: An e-commerce company wants its AI customer service to answer real-time questions about order status. The AI needs access to the order database. Which approach is most appropriate?

stem: When using a foundation model, what is the effect of increasing the temperature parameter?

trap: "Increases determinism" is a distractor; choose "Increases randomness and creativity"

stem: Which prompt technique is best suited for guiding the model to solve complex mathematical reasoning problems?

stem: A company wants a foundation model to better understand medical domain terminology without changing the model's general capabilities. Which method is most appropriate?

stem: What is RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)?

stem: A company's AI application needs to evaluate business alignment metrics. Which of the following is a business alignment metric? (v1.1 new exam point)

stem: Which option best describes the role of Human-in-the-loop in FM evaluation?

stem: What is "Model Distillation"?

hint: Key concept: true positives among all actual positives.
explanation:
In highly imbalanced datasets: Recall (Sensitivity) = TP / (TP + FN), measuring the proportion of all true positives that were successfully identified. In fraud detection or rare disease diagnosis, the cost of missing cases (False Negative) is extremely high, making Recall the priority metric.

Precision measures "what proportion of predicted positives are truly positive."
whyOthersWrong: A) Precision focuses on predicted positives. C) MSE is for regression. D) R-Squared is for regression.
trap: "Precision" is misleading; catching ALL fraud → Recall.
mnemonic: Catch all fraud → Recall

options.text: Controlling model complexity and preventing overfitting

options.text: It processes text sequentially, so it is slower than traditional RNNs but has longer memory

options.label: B
options.text: It computes dot products of Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) matrices, allowing the model to calculate the relevance between any two tokens in the sequence in parallel

options.label: C
options.text: It can only process fixed-length words and cannot perform long text generation

options.label: D
options.text: It primarily relies on convolutional kernels to extract spatial features from images

hint: This is a fundamental GenAI question.
explanation: Self-Attention is the core of Transformers. Through Q, K, V matrices it computes global attention scores, breaking the constraint of RNNs that must process tokens sequentially, greatly improving parallel computation and effectively capturing long-range dependencies.
whyOthersWrong: A) Self-attention enables parallel processing, unlike RNNs. C) Transformers handle variable-length sequences. D) Convolutional kernels are for CNNs, not Transformers.
trap: "Sequential processing" describes RNNs, not Transformers.
mnemonic: Self-Attention: Q·K·V parallel computation → long-range dependencies

stem: In LLM decoding and hyperparameter tuning, if a developer sets Top-P (Nucleus Sampling) to 0.9, what does this mean?

options.label: A
options.text: The model will only randomly select the next token from the top 90% most probable tokens

options.label: B
options.text: The model selects the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches 90%, and samples only from that set

options.label: C
options.text: The model's Temperature is automatically set to 0.9

options.label: D
options.text: The model has a 90% chance of selecting the highest-probability word and 10% chance of selecting a random word each time

hint: This is a fundamental GenAI question.
explanation: Top-P (Nucleus Sampling) dynamically selects candidate tokens by sorting all tokens by probability in descending order, accumulating probabilities until reaching the threshold P (e.g., 0.9), and sampling only from this dynamic set. This is more flexible than fixed Top-K at adapting to probability distributions.
whyOthersWrong: A) It's cumulative probability, not top 90% by count. C) Top-P and Temperature are independent parameters. D) This describes a different sampling mechanism.
trap: "Top 90% of tokens by count" confuses Top-P (cumulative probability) with Top-K (count-based).
mnemonic: Top-P 0.9 = cumulative probability ≤ 90% token set

stem: Which requirement is SageMaker Clarify best suited for?

options.label: A

explanation:
Clarify supports bias detection and explainability.

**Other options / common mistakes:** The others serve different functions.
whyOthersWrong: B) Creating DNS records — that's Route 53. C) Synthesizing speech — that's Amazon Polly. D) Scanning EC2 vulnerabilities — that's Amazon Inspector.
trap: Confusing Clarify with other AWS services.
mnemonic: Clarify = bias + explainability

stem: Which practice best represents transparency in AI systems?

options.label: A
options.text: Inform users they are interacting with AI and disclose its limitations

options.label: B
options.text: Pretend all output is generated by humans

hint: Transparency means letting users know.
explanation:
The AI's usage, limitations, and potential risks should be clearly communicated.

**Other options / common mistakes:** The others contradict transparency principles.
whyOthersWrong: B) Pretend all output is generated by humans — directly opposes transparency. C) Do not record model versions — reduces accountability. D) Hide data sources — reduces verifiability.
trap: Thinking transparency is optional or only about technical documentation.
mnemonic: Transparency = clear disclosure

stem: A model in a medical advice scenario could cause serious consequences. The most appropriate design principle is:

options.label: A
options.text: Retain human oversight for high-risk decisions

options.label: B
options.text: Fully automate with no appeals process

hint: High-impact scenario.
explanation:
Human oversight allows professionals to review model recommendations and intervene in exceptional cases.

**Other options / common mistakes:** B/C/D do not comply with responsible AI.
whyOthersWrong: B) Fully automate with no appeals process — unacceptable for high-risk medical decisions. C) Hide uncertainty — dangerous in healthcare. D) Never log errors — prevents learning and accountability.
trap: Trusting AI fully in high-stakes medical decisions without human oversight.
mnemonic: High risk → Human-in-the-loop

stem: To reduce representational bias in training data, what should the team prioritize?

options.label: A
options.text: Check whether the data covers target populations and supplement underrepresented samples

hint: Start by examining the data.
explanation:
Improving data coverage and representation is a key method for reducing dataset bias.

**Other options / common mistakes:** B doesn't guarantee fairness; C/D worsen governance.
whyOthersWrong: B) Only increase model parameters — larger models don't fix biased data. C) Hide demographic analysis — prevents bias detection. D) Delete the validation set — removes the ability to evaluate bias.
trap: Thinking model size alone can solve data representation issues.
mnemonic: Bias often starts with the data

stem: In Responsible AI, robustness primarily concerns:

options.label: A
options.text: The model's ability to operate reliably under varying conditions, perturbations, or data changes

hint: It's not just about accuracy.
explanation:
Robustness focuses on a model's ability to maintain reasonable performance in the face of noise, distribution shifts, or attacks.

**Other options / common mistakes:** The others don't fit.
whyOthersWrong: B) Whether the logo is consistent — a branding concern, not AI robustness. C) Token unit price — a pricing concern. D) DNS availability — an infrastructure concern.
trap: Confusing robustness with other operational concerns.
mnemonic: Robustness = not easily defeated by environmental changes

stem: A company compares two similarly performing models and wants to reduce energy and compute consumption. This falls under which Responsible AI dimension?
hint: Environmental impact.
explanation:
Sustainability considers the compute, energy, and resource consumption of model training and inference.

**Other options / common mistakes:** The others are unrelated.

trap: Not recognizing environmental impact as a Responsible AI concern.

stem: A Bedrock application needs to read from a specific S3 bucket but should not access other buckets. This best aligns with which principle?

Least privilege grants only the minimum permissions needed to complete the task.

trap: Granting broad permissions for convenience.
mnemonic: Only give what's needed → Least privilege

stem: A company wants to know if a specific IAM principal has called the Bedrock API. Which service should they check?

CloudTrail records AWS API activity and events.

**Other options / common mistakes:** The others don't provide API auditing.
whyOthersWrong: B) Amazon Polly — text-to-speech service. C) Amazon Translate — language translation service. D) Bedrock Prompt Management — manages prompts, not API auditing.
trap: Confusing API auditing with application services.
mnemonic: Who called the API → CloudTrail

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: The security team needs to find files in S3 that may contain credit card numbers and personal information. The best service is:

explanation:
Macie helps discover and classify sensitive data in S3.

Amazon Inspector provides automated vulnerability management and scanning.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: A company needs to obtain AWS SOC and ISO compliance documents. They should use:

AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

AWS Config tracks configuration changes and evaluates compliance against defined rules.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: To protect sensitive data in GenAI applications, which set of measures is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Encryption at rest and in transit, combined with appropriate access controls

hint: Basic security essentials.
explanation:
Sensitive data should use encryption in transit and at rest, combined with least privilege and auditing.

**Other options / common mistakes:** B/C/D increase the risk of data leakage.
whyOthersWrong: B) Make all logs public — exposes potentially sensitive information. C) Give everyone admin access — violates least privilege. D) Disable IAM — removes all access control.
trap: Overlooking the need for layered security measures.
mnemonic: Encrypt + Least privilege + Audit

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: A company is concerned that personal information entered by users could be output by the model to other users. The most important control direction is:

options.label: A
options.text: Data isolation, access control, sensitive information filtering, and appropriate retention policies

explanation:
Data visibility should be restricted, sensitive information filtered, retention managed, and authorization and isolation ensured.

**Other options / common mistakes:** B/C/D are unhelpful or more dangerous.
whyOthersWrong: B) Increase temperature — unrelated to data privacy. C) Increase image resolution — unrelated to PII protection. D) Remove all authentication — makes the problem worse.
trap: Focusing on model parameters instead of data governance.

stem: In the field of computer vision (CV) in machine learning, suppose we want to take a photo containing multiple objects and not only identify which objects are present, but also label every single pixel with the specific object it belongs to (e.g., pixel A belongs to a car, pixel B belongs to the road, pixel C belongs to a pedestrian). What is this type of task called?
hint: Think about which task operates at the pixel level.
explanation: Image segmentation is an advanced computer vision task. Semantic segmentation and instance segmentation classify images at the pixel level, precisely dividing images into different object boundaries and categories. They are widely used in autonomous driving (identifying road/pedestrian pixels) and medical image analysis.
whyOthersWrong: B) Binary Classification only assigns an entire input to one of two classes, not pixel-level labeling. C) Image Resizing changes dimensions without understanding content. D) Text-to-Speech converts text to audio, unrelated to image understanding.
trap: Don't confuse binary classification with segmentation — segmentation works at the pixel level.
mnemonic: Pixel-level labeling → Segmentation

stem: A financial company wants to build a fraud prediction model. Due to regulatory requirements, the model must not be a completely unexplainable black box. The data science team decides to use Feature Importance to show which variables contribute most to fraud detection. Which of the following machine learning algorithms natively supports outputting explicit feature importance scores?

options.label: A
options.text: Random Forest or Gradient Boosted Trees (XGBoost / LightGBM)

hint: This is a fundamental ML concept question.
explanation: Tree-based ensemble learning models (such as Random Forest, XGBoost) natively provide feature importance metrics (e.g., based on Gini Impurity reduction or Feature Gain), which can intuitively show each variable's contribution to model decisions, offering good interpretability.
whyOthersWrong: B) Deep neural networks with many layers are typically black boxes without native feature importance. C) Black-box Autoencoders do not provide interpretable feature rankings. D) Random Samplers are not ML algorithms for prediction.
trap: Don't be misled by 'deep neural network' — depth doesn't mean interpretability.
mnemonic: Trees → Feature Importance

stem: A logistics company wants to predict the incoming and outgoing cargo volume for a specific warehouse over the next week. Since the cargo volume exhibits strong weekly cyclical patterns and seasonal trends, which data type and task should the data team use for modeling?

options.label: A
options.text: Time Series data and Time Series Forecasting task

options.label: B
options.text: Unrelated image data and Image Classification

hint: This is a fundamental ML concept question.
explanation: Data arranged in chronological order with time dependencies (such as periodicity, trends, seasonality) is called Time Series Data. Predicting values at future time points is a time series forecasting task (e.g., using Amazon Forecast or the Prophet algorithm).
whyOthersWrong: B) Image classification is unrelated to temporal prediction. C) Random graph partitioning doesn't handle time-dependent data. D) Audio signal processing is a different domain entirely.
trap: The mention of 'weekly cycles' and 'seasonal trends' is a strong signal for time series.
mnemonic: Weekly cycles + seasonal trends → Time Series Forecasting

stem: When training deep neural networks, what is the core function of an optimizer (e.g., Adam, SGD)?

options.label: A
options.text: Based on gradients computed from the loss function, automatically update the network's weights and biases during backpropagation to minimize the loss

options.label: B
options.text: Automatically send training data to a printer for printing

options.label: D
options.text: Automatically clean dust from the GPU

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: The optimizer is a core component of deep learning training. Based on gradient descent algorithms and backpropagation, it uses the current loss gradient information to adjust model parameters (weights and biases), aiming to find the minimum of the loss function by moving in the opposite direction of the gradient.
whyOthersWrong: B) Printing training data is not a function of any ML component. C) Adding subtitles is a separate application, not an optimizer's role. D) Cleaning GPU dust is a hardware maintenance task, not a software function.
trap: Don't overthink it — the optimizer's job is simply to update weights using gradients.
mnemonic: Optimizer = gradient-based weight updater

stem: In the operation of Large Language Models (LLMs), autoregressive generation relies on the Temperature hyperparameter. When Temperature is set to 0.0, what does the model's generation behavior become?

options.label: A
options.text: The model becomes deterministic, always selecting the highest-probability next token (Greedy Decoding) — the same prompt always produces the exact same response

options.label: B
options.text: The model generates completely random gibberish

options.label: C
options.text: The model refuses to answer any questions

options.label: D
options.text: The model's response length becomes infinite

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: When Temperature is set to 0, the softmax probability distribution degenerates to Greedy Search/Decoding. The model no longer performs any probabilistic sampling and instead selects the top-probability token with 100% certainty. This makes output highly reproducible and deterministic, suitable for SQL generation, math computation, and structured extraction.
whyOthersWrong: B) Temperature 0 produces the most predictable output, not random gibberish. C) The model still responds; it just does so deterministically. D) Temperature does not affect response length.
trap: Don't confuse Temperature 0 (most deterministic) with high Temperature (most random).
mnemonic: Temperature 0 → Greedy Decoding → Deterministic

stem: A prompt engineer is optimizing a prompt using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) technique. What is the core structural characteristic of a CoT prompt?

options.label: A
options.text: Explicitly asking the model to break down and output step-by-step intermediate reasoning before giving the final answer (e.g., 'Please reason step by step...')

options.label: B
options.text: Forcing the model to answer entirely in English

options.label: C
options.text: Copying the prompt 10 times and sending them consecutively

options.label: D
options.text: Requiring the model to include at least 50 meme images in its response

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: The core of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is guiding the LLM to decompose complex problems into a series of intermediate reasoning steps. By asking the model to 'think step by step' or providing examples that include reasoning processes, it can significantly reduce error rates on complex logic, math, and planning tasks.
whyOthersWrong: B) Language choice is unrelated to CoT. C) Repeating prompts does not introduce reasoning steps. D) Including images is unrelated to step-by-step reasoning.
trap: CoT is about reasoning structure, not language or format constraints.
mnemonic: CoT = 'Let's think step by step'

stem: In generative AI, what is the core capability of multimodal embedding models (such as Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings)?

options.label: A
options.text: Mapping text and images simultaneously into the same high-dimensional vector space, so that semantically related text and images have very high vector similarity

options.label: B
options.text: Automatically converting text into Excel formulas

options.label: C
options.text: Converting CPU computations into hard drive backups

options.label: D
options.text: Only capable of processing MIDI music files

hint: Think about how a description of a beach sunset relates to a photo of one.
explanation: Multimodal embedding models project text and images (or other modalities) into a shared embedding space, so that 'a text describing a beach sunset' and 'a photo of a beach sunset' are very close in vector space, enabling cross-modal retrieval like image-to-image or text-to-image search.
whyOthersWrong: B) Converting text to Excel formulas is unrelated to embeddings. C) CPU-to-disk backup is a hardware operation. D) Multimodal models handle multiple modalities, not just MIDI.
trap: The key word is 'shared vector space' — both modalities map to the same representation.
mnemonic: Multimodal embeddings = shared vector space for text + images

stem: Which of the following statements most accurately compares Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Foundation Model Fine-Tuning?

options.label: A
options.text: RAG is suited for static domain style transfer; fine-tuning is suited for real-time database queries

options.label: B
options.text: RAG dynamically retrieves from external knowledge bases during inference without modifying model weights, offering high interpretability and access to up-to-date information; fine-tuning updates model weights via gradient descent, suited for adjusting conversation style, format compliance, and domain-specific terminology

options.label: C
options.text: Fine-tuning can be completed without any training dataset

options.label: D
options.text: RAG's hardware training cost is far higher than full-parameter fine-tuning

hint: Think about which approach modifies model weights and which doesn't.
explanation: RAG does not change model weights. It dynamically injects retrieved up-to-date or private context during inference, making it best practice for providing real-time knowledge, reducing hallucinations, and enabling precise citations. Fine-tuning updates model weights and is suited for adjusting output style, format (e.g., JSON), tone, and absorbing highly specialized domain language.
whyOthersWrong: A) The roles are reversed — RAG handles real-time knowledge, fine-tuning handles style. C) Fine-tuning requires a training dataset by definition. D) RAG has minimal compute cost since it doesn't train; fine-tuning is the expensive one.
trap: Don't swap RAG and fine-tuning roles — RAG retrieves, fine-tuning trains.
mnemonic: RAG = retrieve at inference; Fine-tune = update weights

stem: A company wants to use Llama 3 on Amazon Bedrock to process a large volume of contracts. To prevent prompts from being subject to Prompt Injection attacks, the development team wants to perform security screening before prompts are sent to the LLM. Which native Bedrock feature includes Prompt Attack Defense?
hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails includes dedicated defense filters for Prompt Attacks (prompt injection and jailbreak attempts). It can automatically detect and block injection statements that attempt to bypass system constraints, steal the System Prompt, or execute malicious instructions before the user prompt reaches the foundation model.
whyOthersWrong: B) Knowledge Bases provide RAG retrieval, not prompt security. C) Provisioned Throughput manages capacity, not security. D) Model Customization handles fine-tuning, not attack defense.
trap: Don't confuse Knowledge Bases (retrieval) with Guardrails (safety filters).
mnemonic: Guardrails = safety & prompt attack defense

stem: In LLM fine-tuning techniques, what is the core value of PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning)?

options.label: A
options.text: During fine-tuning, freeze the vast majority of the base model's weights and only train a very small percentage (typically < 1%) of additional parameters, significantly reducing GPU memory requirements, storage, and training costs

options.label: C
options.text: Force the model's output length to be shortened to 1 character

options.label: D
options.text: Can only run on CPUs without any GPU

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, such as LoRA, Prefix Tuning) solves the pain point of traditional full-parameter fine-tuning being too computationally expensive. By freezing most of the original model's weights and only training tiny adapter matrices, PEFT can achieve performance close to full fine-tuning while consuming only a few GB of GPU memory.
whyOthersWrong: B) Deleting all parameters would destroy the model. C) Output length is unrelated to PEFT. D) PEFT still uses GPUs, just fewer resources.
trap: PEFT doesn't remove parameters — it freezes most and trains a small adapter.
mnemonic: PEFT = freeze most, train < 1% adapters

stem: An AI architect is evaluating Decoder-only models using Transformer architecture (such as Claude, GPT-4, Llama) versus Encoder-only models (such as BERT). What is the core strength of Decoder-only models?

options.label: A
options.text: Autoregressive text generation and long-form continuous conversation

options.label: D
options.text: Can only be used for SQL syntax checking

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Transformer Decoder-only architecture uses unidirectional causal/masked self-attention, designed specifically for autoregressive generation. It is the core architecture of all mainstream conversational LLMs (Claude, GPT-4, Llama, Mistral). Encoder-only models (like BERT) specialize in bidirectional semantic understanding and label classification.
whyOthersWrong: B) Decoder-only models generate text, not compress images. C) Single-word fill-in-the-blank is more characteristic of Encoder-only (BERT). D) SQL checking is a specific application, not an architectural strength.
trap: Don't confuse Encoder-only (BERT, understanding) with Decoder-only (GPT, generation).
mnemonic: Decoder-only = autoregressive generation; Encoder-only = understanding

stem: A financial company discovers that when using an LLM to automatically generate investment analysis reports, the model sometimes produces 'confident but completely incorrect stock price data.' To prevent erroneous data from damaging the company's reputation, the team decides to enable Grounding Check in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. How does Grounding Check work?

options.label: A
options.text: Guardrails automatically evaluates whether the model's factual claims are substantively supported by Knowledge Base retrieved documents (grounding). If the model fabricates data, the response is automatically blocked

options.label: B
options.text: Guardrails automatically calls the stock exchange to verify

options.label: C
options.text: Guardrails automatically increases the model's Temperature

options.label: D
options.text: Guardrails automatically translates the report to Japanese

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Grounding Check specifically targets hallucination problems in RAG architectures. It algorithmically cross-checks the model's output sentences against retrieved source documents (context), ensuring every generated fact is backed by evidence. If ungrounded content or fabrication is detected, it is directly blocked or flagged.
whyOthersWrong: B) Guardrails doesn't make external phone calls. C) Increasing Temperature would worsen hallucinations, not reduce them. D) Translation is unrelated to factual grounding.
trap: Grounding Check verifies against retrieved documents, not external sources.
mnemonic: Grounding Check = verify LLM output against retrieved sources

stem: In the tokenization process of generative AI, if the English word 'Unbelievable' is input, the tokenizer might break it into ['Un', 'believ', 'able'] — three tokens. What is the main advantage of this Subword Tokenization technique?

options.label: A
options.text: Able to effectively handle unseen words (out-of-vocabulary words) with a limited vocabulary size while preserving root-word semantics

options.label: B
options.text: Forcibly converts all words to Chinese

options.label: D
options.text: Allows the model to consume zero computational resources

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Subword Tokenization (such as BPE, WordPiece, Unigram) is the standard tokenization method for modern LLMs. It operates between word-level and character-level, breaking rare words into common subword fragments, allowing the model to use a vocabulary of tens of thousands of tokens to flexibly compose and handle any unseen words (OOV) while preserving root and suffix semantic information.
whyOthersWrong: B) Tokenization does not change the language of the text. C) Tokenization segments text, it doesn't eliminate it. D) Tokenization is a preprocessing step that still requires computation.
trap: Subword tokenization balances vocabulary size with coverage of rare words.
mnemonic: Subword = limited vocab handles unlimited words

stem: A law firm wants to use an LLM to process legal case files up to 200 pages long. However, the model's context window is limited to 32K tokens (approximately 100 pages). Which context management strategy would best help the team solve this problem?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a RAG architecture: chunk the 200-page document, vectorize and store in a database, then retrieve only the top 10 most relevant chunks for the current legal question to pass to the model

options.label: B
options.text: Delete half of all documents and upload directly

options.label: C
options.text: Force the model to read 200 pages within 1 second

options.label: D
options.text: Convert the documents to MP3 audio files and send to the model

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: When the total length of source documents exceeds the LLM's context window limit, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is the standard solution. Through chunking and vector retrieval, only the chunks relevant to the user's query are precisely extracted and passed to the LLM, avoiding context window overflow.
whyOthersWrong: B) Deleting content loses critical information. C) Models can't be 'forced' to read faster — it's a token limit. D) Converting to audio doesn't solve the text context window problem.
trap: RAG solves context window limits by retrieving only relevant chunks.
mnemonic: Document too long → Chunk + Retrieve (RAG)

stem: In Amazon Bedrock, when a developer chooses to call Foundation Models using On-Demand mode, how are API rate limits (such as Requests Per Minute or Tokens Per Minute) managed?

options.label: A
options.text: Each AWS account has default service quotas per region per model. Exceeding the quota returns a ThrottlingException (HTTP 429). Users can request quota increases or switch to Provisioned Throughput

options.label: B
options.text: On-demand mode has no rate limits and allows unlimited concurrency

options.label: C
options.text: When limits are exceeded, AWS automatically deletes the customer's account

options.label: D
options.text: Rate limits are determined by the user's computer hard drive speed

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Amazon Bedrock On-Demand mode is governed by AWS Service Quotas, with RPM (Requests Per Minute) and TPM (Tokens Per Minute) limits set for each model. If an application's concurrency exceeds the quota, Bedrock throws a ThrottlingException (429). Enterprises can request increases through the Service Quotas console or purchase Provisioned Throughput.
whyOthersWrong: B) All AWS services have rate limits. C) AWS never auto-deletes accounts for exceeding quotas. D) Rate limits are server-side, not client hardware-dependent.
trap: On-demand doesn't mean unlimited — quotas still apply.
mnemonic: On-Demand → Service Quotas → 429 ThrottlingException

stem: Which metric is most commonly used to evaluate the image quality and realism of generative AI image generation models (such as Stable Diffusion), comparing the distribution of generated images against the distribution of real images?
hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) is the gold standard metric for evaluating image generation models (GANs, Diffusion Models). It extracts feature vectors from both real and generated image sets using the Inception network and computes the Fréchet distance between their multivariate Gaussian distributions. A lower FID score indicates more realistic generated images that more closely match the real image distribution.
whyOthersWrong: B) ROUGE-L evaluates text summarization, not image quality. C) BLEU-4 evaluates machine translation quality. D) F1-Score evaluates classification performance.
trap: ROUGE and BLEU are for text; FID is for images.
mnemonic: Image quality → FID; Text quality → ROUGE/BLEU

stem: In Prompt Engineering, what is the main difference between a System Prompt and a User Prompt?

options.label: A
options.text: The System Prompt sets the model's overall role, behavioral rules, and safety boundaries; the User Prompt is the specific question or instruction the user inputs during a particular conversation

options.label: B
options.text: The System Prompt is auto-generated by the model; the User Prompt is written by AWS system administrators

options.label: C
options.text: The System Prompt can only contain binary code; the User Prompt can only contain French

options.label: D
options.text: The two are completely identical with no difference

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: The System Prompt establishes the LLM's overall behavioral constraints, persona, output format guidelines, and refusal boundaries (it is a meta-instruction passed to the model at the very beginning of a conversation). The User Prompt is the specific query or task request initiated by the user during interaction.
whyOthersWrong: B) System Prompts are written by developers, not auto-generated. C) Both prompts are natural language text with no format restrictions. D) They serve fundamentally different purposes.
trap: System Prompt = persistent role/rules; User Prompt = per-turn input.
mnemonic: System = role & rules; User = question & tasks

stem: A biotech company wants to use AI to automatically generate novel antibody protein sequences. The team decides to use Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) or rule-based reward functions to align the model. What is the primary meaning of 'alignment' in foundation model development?

options.label: A
options.text: Adjusting the pre-trained model's behavior and outputs to conform to human expectations, safety standards, ethical guidelines, and domain-specific preferences

options.label: B
options.text: Aligning all text output boundaries to the left side of the screen

options.label: C
options.text: Arranging GPU server racks in a straight line

options.label: D
options.text: Making the model file size align to multiples of 1GB

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Model alignment refers to using techniques like SFT, RLHF, and DPO to guide large-scale pre-trained models (which originally only have the ability to predict the next token) so their output behavior conforms to human intent, safety standards, honesty, and specific domain norms (Helpful, Honest, Harmless).
whyOthersWrong: B) Text alignment on screen is a display/CSS concept, not AI alignment. C) Physical rack arrangement is unrelated. D) File size rounding is a storage concern, not model behavior.
trap: AI alignment is about behavior and values, not physical or visual alignment.
mnemonic: Alignment = Helpful, Honest, Harmless (HHH)

stem: In the 2026 updated exam guide, the Agentic AI domain introduces Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents concepts. What is the core mechanism of Tool Use / Function Calling in an Agentic AI architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: During inference, the LLM recognizes when it needs external data or actions, automatically outputs structured API call parameters (e.g., JSON), and an orchestration framework executes the API and returns results to the LLM for the next reasoning step

options.label: B
options.text: The LLM directly takes over the server's OS kernel and automatically reinstalls Windows

options.label: C
options.text: The LLM automatically dispatches physical robots to repair computers at client locations

options.label: D
options.text: The LLM automatically downloads data to a USB drive

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Tool Use / Function Calling allows the LLM to act as the system's brain. When the LLM determines it cannot answer using only its internal knowledge, it outputs a formatted structure (e.g., JSON with API name and parameters). The application framework (such as Bedrock Agent) executes the API, feeds results back to the LLM, and the LLM integrates the results to provide a final answer.
whyOthersWrong: B) LLMs don't control operating systems directly. C) LLMs don't dispatch physical robots. D) LLMs don't interact with physical USB hardware.
trap: Tool Use is about structured API calls, not direct system control.
mnemonic: Tool Use = LLM outputs JSON → Framework executes → Results fed back

stem: A developer calling the Amazon Bedrock API passes the Top-K hyperparameter. If Top-K is set to 1, what does this mean?

options.label: A
options.text: When predicting the next token, the model always selects from only the 1 highest-probability token (i.e., Greedy Search)

options.label: C
options.text: Each API call costs only 1 cent

options.label: D
options.text: The model can only process sentences of 1 word

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question.
explanation: Top-K sampling limits the model to sample only from the top K highest-probability candidate tokens when predicting the next token. When Top-K is set to 1, the candidate pool contains only the single highest-probability token, producing the same effect as Top-P = 0 or Temperature = 0 — Greedy Search.
whyOthersWrong: B) Top-K=1 produces one deterministic response, not 100. C) Top-K controls sampling strategy, not pricing. D) Top-K controls token selection, not input length.
trap: Top-K=1 is equivalent to greedy decoding — most deterministic output.
mnemonic: Top-K=1 → only pick the #1 token → Greedy Search

stem: Regarding the comparison between Fine-Tuning and Prompt Engineering in reducing LLM hallucinations, which statement is MOST accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Prompt Engineering combined with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is generally more effective at reducing factual hallucinations than fine-tuning alone, because RAG provides the model with instantly verifiable contextual evidence

options.label: B
options.text: Fine-tuning alone can 100% completely eliminate all hallucinations, while RAG cannot

options.label: C
options.text: Prompt Engineering cannot have any impact on a model's responses

options.label: D
options.text: Fine-tuning does not require any GPU to complete

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question
explanation: Research and practice show that while fine-tuning can change a model's style and vocabulary, it cannot fully eliminate factual hallucinations (and may even introduce them due to fuzzy memorization). Combining Prompt Engineering with RAG (providing retrieved up-to-date factual context) is currently the most cost-effective and reliable method for suppressing hallucinations.
whyOthersWrong: B) Fine-tuning cannot 100% eliminate all hallucinations — this is a false claim. C) Prompt Engineering clearly influences model responses through context and instructions. D) Fine-tuning requires significant GPU compute resources.
trap: Confusing fine-tuning's ability to change style with its ability to eliminate hallucinations — choose the RAG + Prompt Engineering combination
mnemonic: RAG + Prompting = best hallucination defense

stem: A company wants to use Amazon Bedrock to build a multilingual customer service bot. During testing, the team wants to evaluate whether the model's Japanese responses are fluent and conform to Japanese grammar conventions. Besides human evaluation, which LLM-as-a-Judge method can the team use for automated evaluation?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a more capable large model (such as Claude 3.5 Sonnet) with specific scoring rubrics to automatically rate the target model's response quality on a 1-to-5 scale and generate feedback

options.label: B
options.text: Use SQL SELECT syntax to check grammar

options.label: C
options.text: Convert Japanese text to binary code and count the number of 1s

options.label: D
options.text: Use a hard drive scanning tool

hint: This is a GenAI fundamentals question
explanation: LLM-as-a-Judge is a cutting-edge practice in generative AI evaluation. By prompting a powerful top-tier foundation model (such as Claude 3.5 Sonnet) with clear scoring rubrics, the strong model can automatically score the evaluated model's output (for fluency, compliance, factuality) and provide reasoning, achieving high consistency with human scoring.
whyOthersWrong: B) SQL syntax has nothing to do with natural language quality evaluation. C) Converting to binary is completely irrelevant to language fluency assessment. D) Hard drive scanning tools are for storage diagnostics, not language evaluation.
trap: Don't confuse data processing tools with AI evaluation methods — LLM-as-a-Judge uses a stronger model to evaluate a weaker one
mnemonic: LLM-as-a-Judge: strong model scores weak model

stem: In generative AI, what is the core input that controls the direction of content generation in Diffusion Models when generating images?

options.label: A
options.text: Natural language text prompts or conditioning control matrices (ControlNet / Conditioning Vector)

hint: Think about what drives conditional generation in diffusion models
explanation: Diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion, Amazon Titan Image Generator) use a conditional generation mechanism. The user's text prompt is converted into a conditioning vector through a Text Encoder (such as CLIP), which guides the denoising network (UNet) to produce images matching the prompt's semantics during the denoising process.
whyOthersWrong: B) MAC addresses are network identifiers, unrelated to image generation. C) Credit card numbers are financial data with no relevance to AI model inputs. D) Database table structures are for data storage, not image generation control.
trap: Don't confuse IT infrastructure concepts with AI model inputs — diffusion models are guided by text prompts and conditioning vectors
mnemonic: Diffusion = Text Prompt → CLIP → Conditioning Vector → UNet

stem: A multinational financial institution wants to build a highly reliable financial report analysis system using Amazon Bedrock. Due to extremely high traffic, the company has purchased Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput. Which statement about Provisioned Throughput is MOST accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Provides dedicated Model Units (MUs) compute resources, ensuring stable high throughput and low latency, and grants a dedicated model ARN for API calls

options.label: B
options.text: Provisioned Throughput only applies to image generation models, not text models

options.label: C
options.text: Provisioned Throughput publishes the model on the public internet for everyone to use for free

options.label: D
options.text: Provisioned Throughput does not support any data encryption

hint: Think about what dedicated compute resources provide
explanation: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput allows customers to reserve Model Units (MUs), gaining dedicated high-throughput guarantees unaffected by public API rate limits, and generates a dedicated Provisioned Model ARN for API calls, suitable for enterprise-grade critical production workloads.
whyOthersWrong: B) Provisioned Throughput applies to both text and image models. C) Provisioned models remain private and secure, not publicly accessible. D) All AWS services support encryption; Provisioned Throughput is no exception.
trap: Don't confuse Provisioned Throughput scope — it works across model types, not just image generation
mnemonic: Provisioned Throughput = dedicated MUs + dedicated ARN + no rate limits

stem: An insurance company wants to build a claims inquiry system based on Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The company's claims policy documents contain many large cross-reference tables. To ensure that the logical relationships between rows and columns are not lost after vectorization, which document parsing strategy should the team choose?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable the Amazon Textract integration parsing strategy (Advanced Parsing with Amazon Textract)

options.label: B
options.text: Use the default plain text parser

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically convert all PDFs to MP3 audio

hint: Think about which AWS service specializes in document structure extraction
explanation: Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports Advanced Parsing with built-in Amazon Textract integration. When documents contain complex tables, multi-column layouts, or charts, Textract Parsing can precisely reconstruct the table structure and semantic relationships, significantly improving retrieval and answer accuracy.
whyOthersWrong: B) The default plain text parser strips table structure, losing row-column relationships. C) Converting PDFs to audio is irrelevant to document parsing. D) Deleting tables removes valuable data instead of preserving it.
trap: Don't assume the default parser handles tables well — complex tables need Textract's advanced parsing
mnemonic: Complex tables → Textract Advanced Parsing

stem: A healthcare technology company wants to fine-tune and deploy an open-source medical LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI. To protect patient privacy and comply with HIPAA, the company requires that traffic between the SageMaker inference endpoint and the S3 bucket storing training data must be completely enclosed within the AWS internal network, never traversing the public internet. What network architecture should the architect configure?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure Amazon VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink) and deploy SageMaker training and inference jobs in designated private subnets with EnableNetworkIsolation enabled

options.label: B
options.text: Set the SageMaker endpoint to Public Unauthenticated Access

hint: Think about how to keep traffic within the AWS private network
explanation: In Amazon SageMaker, by deploying containers in VPC private subnets, configuring VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink), and enabling EnableNetworkIsolation in training/inference jobs, you can completely cut off container access to the public internet, ensuring data stays within the AWS private backbone network.
whyOthersWrong: B) Public unauthenticated access directly contradicts the HIPAA privacy requirement. C) Home Wi-Fi is irrelevant to AWS network architecture. D) Disabling VPC services removes the network isolation capability needed for compliance.
trap: Don't confuse public access with private network isolation — HIPAA requires traffic to stay within AWS
mnemonic: HIPAA + SageMaker = VPC Endpoints + Private Subnets + NetworkIsolation

options.label: A
options.text: Through associated Action Groups that trigger corresponding AWS Lambda functions

options.label: B
options.text: By sending an email to a customer service agent for manual processing

options.label: C
options.text: By popping up a console window for the customer to manually enter SQL code

options.label: D
options.text: The Agent cannot execute any external actions

hint: Think about how Bedrock Agents interact with external systems
explanation: Amazon Bedrock Agents interact with external systems through Action Groups. Each Action Group is bound to an AWS Lambda function. When the Agent reasons that a specific action needs to be executed (such as querying a database or generating a logistics label), it automatically assembles parameters and invokes the corresponding Lambda function to execute the business logic.
whyOthersWrong: B) Bedrock Agents automate actions programmatically, not through manual email workflows. C) Agents don't require customers to write SQL — they handle data access through Lambda. D) Agents are specifically designed to execute external actions via Action Groups.
trap: Don't think Bedrock Agents are limited to text generation — they can take real actions through Action Groups + Lambda
mnemonic: Bedrock Agent actions = Action Groups → Lambda functions

stem: A news media company wants to perform batch semantic vectorization (embedding) on 5 million news articles from the past 10 years and store them in a vector database. Due to the enormous volume, using On-Demand real-time API calls would be expensive and likely trigger rate limits. What is the MOST suitable and cost-effective Amazon Bedrock processing mode?
hint: Think about which processing mode is designed for large-scale non-real-time tasks
explanation: Amazon Bedrock Batch Inference is designed specifically for large-scale, non-real-time data processing tasks (such as mass text summarization, bulk vectorization, data labeling). Users simply upload request files to S3 for batch processing, which is typically 50% cheaper than On-Demand mode and not subject to real-time API rate limits.
whyOthersWrong: B) Real-time streaming is designed for interactive use cases, not bulk processing. C) Amazon Lex is a chatbot service, not a batch embedding tool. D) Manual single-article invocation is impractical for 5 million articles and doesn't solve the cost/rate-limit problem.
trap: Don't confuse real-time and batch inference modes — batch is specifically for high-volume, non-urgent workloads
mnemonic: 5 million articles → Batch Inference (50% cheaper, no rate limits)

stem: An AI system architect is building a RAG system using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. When users search for 'invoice refund process', the system retrieves many document chunks containing the keywords 'invoice' or 'refund' but with irrelevant content. To improve retrieval precision, the architect wants to perform secondary fine-grained scoring and reranking on the top 50 candidate chunks after the initial vector search, selecting the truly most relevant top 5 chunks. Which type of model should be added?
hint: Think about what model type performs secondary scoring on retrieval candidates
explanation: Reranking models are a key component for optimizing RAG retrieval quality. While vector search excels at quickly filtering top-N candidates from millions of documents, rerank models use deep cross-attention mechanisms to perform fine-grained semantic relevance scoring between the N candidate chunks and the query, significantly improving the quality of context sent to the LLM.
whyOthersWrong: B) Image Classification is for visual content, not text retrieval quality. C) Speech-to-Text converts audio to text, irrelevant to document retrieval reranking.
trap: Don't confuse different AI model types — reranking specifically addresses retrieval precision in RAG pipelines
mnemonic: Vector search (fast recall) → Reranker (precise relevance) → LLM

stem: Which AWS managed service provides pre-trained computer vision APIs that can automatically perform Content Moderation, Face Liveness Detection, and Text Detection in Images for both images and videos?
hint: Think about which AWS service specializes in image and video analysis
explanation: Amazon Rekognition is a managed computer vision service that provides ready-to-use APIs for image and video moderation (detecting adult/violent content), face recognition and liveness detection, celebrity identification, and text detection in images, among other visual AI capabilities.
whyOthersWrong: B) Amazon Transcribe is a speech-to-text service, not computer vision. C) Amazon Titan Text Embeddings is for text vectorization, not image analysis. D) Amazon Kendra is an enterprise search service, not a visual AI service.
trap: Don't confuse AWS AI services — Rekognition is specifically for computer vision tasks
mnemonic: Rekognition = vision (images + video + faces + text-in-image)

stem: A financial company wants to deploy an AI customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock. The company's compliance department requires that when a customer asks sensitive questions during a conversation (e.g., 'How can I bypass the bank's anti-money laundering review?'), the system must immediately block the response and log the violation event. Which native Amazon Bedrock security feature should the development team configure?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (configure Denied Topics and Guardrails Logging)

hint: Think about which Bedrock feature handles content safety and topic filtering
explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails allows developers to set up Denied Topics (such as money laundering, illegal activities) and content filters. When a block is triggered, Guardrails automatically intercepts the response and can log violations (Invocation Logs) to S3/CloudWatch, fully meeting financial compliance audit requirements.
whyOthersWrong: B) S3 Lifecycle Rules manage object storage retention, not content filtering. C) AWS Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection service. D) CloudFront Edge Locations are for content delivery, not AI safety.
trap: Don't confuse infrastructure services with AI safety features — Guardrails is purpose-built for content control
mnemonic: Sensitive topics + compliance logging = Bedrock Guardrails

stem: A software company deploying open-source LLMs on Amazon SageMaker AI wants to maximize GPU utilization and reduce per-inference cost. The team decides to use dynamic/continuous batching technology based on vLLM or TGI (Text Generation Inference). What is the core advantage of Continuous Batching?

options.label: A
options.text: Dynamically inserts newly arrived requests and removes completed requests at the iteration level, eliminating GPU idle time caused by traditional Static Batching, significantly improving throughput

options.label: B
options.text: Reduces GPU hardware temperature by 50 degrees

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically deletes duplicate users from the database

options.label: D
options.text: Reduces the model's parameter count by 100x

hint: Think about how continuous batching differs from static batching at the scheduling level
explanation: Continuous Batching (as used by vLLM/TGI) is a major breakthrough in LLM inference optimization. Unlike traditional Static Batching that must wait for the longest sequence in a batch to complete before processing new requests, Continuous Batching dynamically schedules at every token iteration level, dramatically improving GPU utilization and requests per second (RPS).
whyOthersWrong: B) Continuous Batching is about compute scheduling, not hardware temperature. C) Database user management is unrelated to inference optimization. D) Model parameter count is determined by architecture, not batching strategy.
trap: Don't confuse inference scheduling optimization with model compression or hardware management
mnemonic: Continuous Batching = iteration-level scheduling → no GPU idle time

stem: Regarding Amazon Bedrock's Model Evaluation feature, which statement is MOST accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Supports automated evaluation (calculating metrics such as accuracy, toxicity, and filtering) as well as human evaluation (bringing in internal teams or AWS experts for scoring), helping enterprises select the most suitable FM for their specific business scenarios

options.label: B
options.text: Can only be used to evaluate the power consumption of hardware servers

options.label: C
options.text: The evaluation process automatically exposes all of the customer's private data

options.label: D
options.text: Can only evaluate text models, not multimodal models

hint: Think about the two types of evaluation workflows Bedrock offers
explanation: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation provides a fully managed model evaluation workflow. Developers can use default or custom datasets to quantitatively compare different models through automated metrics (such as Accuracy, Robustness, Toxicity) or human evaluation workflows, assisting with model selection.
whyOthersWrong: B) Model Evaluation assesses AI model quality, not hardware power consumption. C) Customer data privacy is protected; evaluation doesn't expose private data. D) Bedrock Model Evaluation supports both text and multimodal models.
trap: Don't limit your understanding of Model Evaluation to text only — it covers multiple modalities
mnemonic: Bedrock Model Eval = automated metrics + human evaluation workflows

stem: A company wants to integrate Amazon Bedrock into its internal applications. The development team wants to ensure that all API requests use the most secure encryption protocol during transmission. What is the default and enforced transport encryption standard for Amazon Bedrock API endpoints?
hint: Think about the standard encryption protocol AWS enforces on all service endpoints
explanation: All AWS service endpoints (including Amazon Bedrock API) mandate secure HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or higher) for encryption in transit. Any unencrypted HTTP request is directly rejected by the AWS API Gateway/Endpoint.
whyOthersWrong: B) Plaintext HTTP is rejected by AWS endpoints — all traffic must be encrypted. C) FTP is an insecure file transfer protocol, not used for API communication. D) Bluetooth is a short-range wireless protocol, completely irrelevant to cloud API security.
trap: This is straightforward — all AWS APIs enforce HTTPS/TLS, no exceptions
mnemonic: AWS API = always HTTPS (TLS 1.2+)

stem: A game development company wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI to fine-tune an image generation model. The training process requires 8 servers, each with 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs (64 GPUs total), working in high coordination. To ensure ultra-high bandwidth, low-latency RDMA network interconnection between nodes, which dedicated SageMaker infrastructure architecture should the company use?

options.label: A
options.text: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod (with EFA Elastic Fabric Adapter networking)

hint: Think about which SageMaker feature is built for large-scale distributed GPU training
explanation: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is AWS's dedicated high-performance infrastructure built specifically for large-scale generative AI and LLM training. It comes pre-configured with distributed training clusters, supports EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter) low-latency RDMA networking, and has the ability to automatically detect and repair faulty nodes, ensuring uninterrupted large-scale GPU training.
whyOthersWrong: B) Serverless Inference is for lightweight inference workloads, not large-scale distributed training. C) S3 Standard is object storage, not compute infrastructure. D) Storage Gateway bridges on-premises storage with AWS, unrelated to GPU training.
trap: Don't confuse inference services with training infrastructure — HyperPod is specifically for large-scale distributed training
mnemonic: 64 GPUs + RDMA = SageMaker HyperPod + EFA

stem: An AI engineer has created a Custom Model (fine-tuned model) in the Amazon Bedrock console. After fine-tuning is complete, the engineer wants to use the custom model for real-time API calls. What step must be performed to obtain the corresponding API call endpoint?

options.label: A
options.text: Purchase/configure Provisioned Throughput for the Custom Model to obtain a dedicated model Endpoint ARN

options.label: B
options.text: Download the model files to a USB drive and run it manually

options.label: C
options.text: Send the model via email to AWS customer service

options.label: D
options.text: Custom models cannot make API calls

hint: Think about what's required to serve a fine-tuned Bedrock model
explanation: In Amazon Bedrock, after completing Custom Model (fine-tuned model) training, Provisioned Throughput must be configured for the custom model to perform real-time inference. This generates a dedicated Provisioned Model ARN for applications to make InvokeModel API calls.
whyOthersWrong: B) Bedrock models are served through managed API endpoints, not downloaded to USB drives. C) Model deployment is self-service through the console/API, not via email. D) Custom models absolutely can make API calls once Provisioned Throughput is configured.
trap: Remember that Bedrock custom models require Provisioned Throughput — they can't use On-Demand like base models
mnemonic: Custom Model → Provisioned Throughput → Endpoint ARN → InvokeModel

stem: In responsible AI governance, when an AI system produces unfair decisions against certain specific communities due to bias in the training data, which core principle of responsible AI is being violated?
hint: Think about which responsible AI principle addresses bias and equitable treatment
explanation: Fairness is a foundational pillar of responsible AI. It requires that AI system decisions should not cause bias, discrimination, or unfair treatment of specific groups based on sensitive attributes (such as race, gender, age, religion, disability, etc.).
whyOthersWrong: B) System Throughput is a performance metric, not a responsible AI principle. C) Hardware Cooling is an infrastructure concern, not an ethical principle. D) Network Bandwidth is a connectivity metric, not related to AI fairness.
trap: Don't confuse technical infrastructure metrics with responsible AI principles
mnemonic: Biased training data → unfair decisions → Fairness principle violated

stem: A healthcare technology company is using GenAI to build an AI-assisted medical consultation system. To prevent the AI from providing potentially fatal incorrect medication recommendations, the company architect designed this mechanism: the AI system can only generate 'draft recommendations', and the draft must be reviewed and signed off by a qualified attending physician in the system before it can be sent to the pharmacy for prescription. Which type of responsible AI control measure does this represent?
hint: Think about which control mechanism requires human expert approval before critical AI decisions take effect
explanation: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) ensures that high-risk AI applications (such as medical prescriptions, legal rulings, high-value loans) don't cause serious consequences due to AI hallucinations or errors, by introducing human expert review and approval at critical decision points. It is a core mechanism for ensuring Safety and Accountability.
whyOthersWrong: B) Unmanned Autopilot removes human oversight, the opposite of what's described. C) A disclaimer doesn't prevent harmful outputs — it just tries to limit legal liability. D) Network firewall rules are for network security, not AI decision safety.
trap: The key indicator is 'draft must be approved by a human expert before execution' — that's textbook HITL
mnemonic: AI draft → human expert approval → action = Human-in-the-Loop

stem: After launching an AI automated loan approval system, a financial company received customer complaints alleging unfair rejection by the system. The company used Amazon SageMaker Clarify to output SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) feature contribution values, clearly explaining to the customer that the rejection reason was '3 late payment records in the past 12 months'. Which pillar of responsible AI does this primarily demonstrate?
hint: Think about which responsible AI principle is demonstrated when AI decisions can be explained to stakeholders
explanation: Explainability and Transparency require AI systems to be able to explain the logic and key influencing factors behind their predictions and decisions to stakeholders. Quantifying each feature's impact on the prediction through SHAP values is a standard engineering practice for implementing Explainable AI (XAI).
whyOthersWrong: B) Server hardware backup is an infrastructure concern, not a responsible AI principle. C) Model network acceleration is about performance, not explainability. D) Server power-saving mode is an operational concern, not related to AI transparency.
trap: SHAP values + explaining decisions to customers = Explainability & Transparency, not just any responsible AI principle
mnemonic: SHAP feature contributions → explain why → Explainability & Transparency

stem: Under the Safety principle of responsible AI, preventing generative AI from being used by malicious actors to write bioweapon manufacturing guides or hacking tools typically requires which two control measures during model development and deployment?

options.label: A
options.text: Safety Alignment training (RLHF) and inference-stage safety guardrails (Guardrails / Safety Filters)

options.label: B
options.text: Publishing the model code entirely on a public forum

hint: Think about the two stages where AI safety controls are applied — training and inference
explanation: Preventing GenAI from generating dangerous or harmful content (CBRN, cyberattacks, self-harm, etc.) uses a dual defense: 1. Safety Alignment during training through RLHF/DPO; 2. Dynamic input/output filtering during inference through deployed Guardrails (such as Bedrock Guardrails).
whyOthersWrong: B) Publishing model code publicly increases risk rather than mitigating it. C) Disabling security checks is the opposite of what's needed for safety. D) Home Wi-Fi is irrelevant to AI content safety controls.
trap: Remember both layers of defense: training-time alignment AND inference-time guardrails
mnemonic: Safety = RLHF (training) + Guardrails (inference) = dual defense

stem: Rank the following four foundation model customization approaches from lowest to highest cost:
hint: Think about which approach requires absolutely no parameter training.
explanation: ICL only requires adding examples to the prompt — zero training cost, making it the cheapest. RAG requires building a vector database but doesn't train the model. Fine-tuning requires labeled data and GPU training. Pre-training trains an entire model from scratch, making it the most expensive.
whyOthersWrong: A common mistake is ranking RAG before ICL, but RAG requires building and maintaining a knowledge base (vector database, embedding model), whereas ICL only requires modifying the prompt.
trap: It's easy to think RAG is 'free' because it doesn't train the model, but the ongoing costs of the data retrieval pipeline, vector database, and embedding computation are often overlooked.
mnemonic: Cost order: 'ICL writes prompt → RAG queries data → FT trains model → PT builds model'

stem: Rank the following four foundation model customization approaches from lowest to highest implementation complexity:
hint: Which one only requires modifying the prompt with no additional infrastructure?
explanation: ICL only requires modifying the prompt — simplest. RAG needs a document processing pipeline, vector database, and retrieval logic. Fine-tuning requires preparing training data, setting up training environments, and tuning hyperparameters. Pre-training requires massive datasets, distributed training clusters, and months of time.
whyOthersWrong: Fine-tuning on Bedrock may seem simple (a few UI clicks), but preparing high-quality labeled data is where the real complexity lies.
trap: Bedrock's UI makes fine-tuning 'look' simple, but the actual data preparation, format conversion, validation, and hyperparameter tuning are the real engineering challenges.
mnemonic: Complexity order: 'modify prompt → connect data → train parameters → build model'

stem: Rank the following four customization approaches from least to most training data required:
hint: How many examples does ICL need? What does RAG require? How much labeled data does fine-tuning need?
explanation: ICL only needs a few examples in the prompt (typically 3–10). RAG needs knowledge base documents (which can be unstructured). Fine-tuning requires hundreds to thousands of high-quality labeled data points. Pre-training needs billions of tokens from a massive corpus.
whyOthersWrong: RAG data doesn't need to be 'labeled' — it just needs to be valuable documents. Fine-tuning, on the other hand, requires carefully labeled input-output pairs.
trap: Don't confuse RAG's 'knowledge base document volume' with fine-tuning's 'labeled training data' — the former can be large but doesn't require human labeling, while every piece of the latter must be labeled.
mnemonic: Data volume order: 'a few examples → document library → labeled dataset → corpus'

stem: A law firm wants its AI assistant to answer questions about the latest regulatory amendments. Regulations are updated quarterly, and the firm does not want to retrain the model. What is the most appropriate customization approach?
hint: The key words are 'latest' and 'does not want to retrain.'
explanation: RAG allows the model to retrieve up-to-date documents at inference time without retraining. Since regulations are updated quarterly, only the knowledge base needs to be refreshed with RAG.
whyOthersWrong: Both pre-training and fine-tuning require retraining, which conflicts with the 'no retraining' requirement. ICL cannot handle large volumes of regulatory documents due to prompt length limitations.
trap: Seeing 'legal domain' might make you choose fine-tuning, but the question emphasizes 'latest' and 'no retraining' — those are the key factors pointing to RAG.
mnemonic: 'Latest data + no retraining = RAG'

stem: A healthcare company has 5,000 labeled radiology reports (X-ray image descriptions → diagnostic recommendations) and wants the model to produce reports that match the hospital's specific format and terminology. What is the most appropriate customization approach?
hint: Notice the two conditions: labeled data is available, and the model's output style needs to change.
explanation: Fine-tuning is ideal when sufficient labeled data is available and the model's behavior or style needs to change. The 5,000 labeled reports are enough for fine-tuning, and the goal is for the model to 'learn' the specific report format and medical terminology.
whyOthersWrong: ICL with a few examples cannot fully teach the model professional formatting. RAG retrieves information but doesn't change the model's writing style. Pre-training is overkill and lacks sufficient data.
trap: Seeing 'medical' might make you choose RAG (query a knowledge base), but the question asks for 'changing output format and terminology' — that's a behavior change, not knowledge retrieval.
mnemonic: 'Labeled data + change style = Fine-tuning'

stem: Rank the following four customization approaches from lowest to highest inference latency:
hint: Which one requires an additional retrieval step during inference? Which one increases latency due to a longer prompt?
explanation: The original pre-trained model is fastest (no extra processing). A fine-tuned model has the same inference speed (weights are internalized). ICL increases context length by adding examples to the prompt, making it slightly slower. RAG requires retrieving documents before generation — an extra step making it the slowest.
whyOthersWrong: A common mistake is thinking a fine-tuned model is slower than the original — in fact, inference speed remains the same after fine-tuning; only the weights differ.
trap: Fine-tuning 'training' is slow, but 'inference' is just as fast as the original model. Don't confuse training time with inference latency.
mnemonic: Latency order: 'original fastest → fine-tuned same → ICL longer → RAG extra step'

stem: Which statement most correctly distinguishes the use cases for RAG and fine-tuning?

options.label: A
options.text: RAG is suited for scenarios requiring the latest external knowledge; fine-tuning is suited for scenarios requiring changes to model behavior or style

options.label: B
options.text: RAG always has higher accuracy than fine-tuning

options.label: C
options.text: Fine-tuning does not require any training data

options.label: D
options.text: RAG and fine-tuning are mutually exclusive and cannot be used together

hint: Think: RAG solves 'knowledge' problems, while fine-tuning solves 'behavior' problems.
explanation: RAG retrieves external knowledge to help the model answer questions about up-to-date information (knowledge dimension). Fine-tuning changes the model's output style and behavior through additional training (behavior dimension). The two can be used in combination.
whyOthersWrong: B is not always true — it depends on the scenario and data quality. C is incorrect — fine-tuning requires labeled data. D is incorrect — RAG + fine-tuning can be used together (fine-tune first, then add RAG).
trap: Candidates who choose D overlook the 'RAG + fine-tuning' combination pattern — fine-tune to improve the model's base capabilities, then use RAG to supplement with up-to-date knowledge.
mnemonic: 'RAG supplements knowledge, FT changes behavior, they can be used together'

stem: Rank the following four customization approaches from shortest to longest time from start to production:
hint: Which one can go live immediately after modifying the prompt?
explanation: ICL only requires modifying the prompt — can go live in minutes. RAG needs a knowledge base and retrieval pipeline to be built — typically days to weeks. Fine-tuning requires data preparation, training, and evaluation — typically weeks. Pre-training requires months of data preparation and training.
whyOthersWrong: RAG may seem simple, but a 'complete knowledge base' involves document processing, chunking, embedding, vector storage, and retrieval logic — each step takes engineering time.
trap: Using Bedrock Knowledge Base can speed up RAG deployment, but it still requires document preparation and testing — it's not 'instant.'
mnemonic: Time-to-production: 'prompt change = minutes → RAG = days → FT = weeks → PT = months'

stem:
An e-commerce company has three AI requirements. Select the best customization approach pairing:
(1) A customer service bot needs to answer questions about the latest return policy
(2) Product description generation needs to match the brand's tone of voice
